newsitem.title: USA: No more victims found in Houston wall collapse.
newsitem.headline: No more victims found in Houston wall collapse.

text.p: Rescue workers reported finding no more victims on Friday under mounds of rubble from a collapsed wall that killed three people during renovations at a Houston mall, officials said.

Up to six were initially believed missing on Thursday after the wall collapsed on people walking in the mall for exercise, but Houston Fire Department spokesman Rick Flanagan said crews clearing away the remaining debris found no more bodies.
"We've pulled our crews out. The rubble's been cleared and there were no more victims in there," Flanagan said.
State and federal investigators have started a probe into the accident.
Firefighters pulled the bodies of three women out of the rubble at the Northline mall on Thursday and 60 rescue workers searched through the debris overnight looking for any more victims.

The 20-foot-tall (six-metre-tall) wall collapsed as demolition teams were tearing down a vacant department store to make way for a 12-screen movie theater to be built by a company owned by former basketball star Earvin "Magic" Johnson.

Six people were also injured as concrete beams from the roof gave way and a two-story walkway fell on the early morning walkers, officials said. Crews used three large cranes to remove the concrete beams.

Since the mall opened in March 1963 there have been three other structural collapses, including one three weeks after the mall opened in which a section of roof gave way under the weight of accumulated rainwater. No one was killed or injured in the earlier accidents, the Houston Chronicle reported.
